title: Where Did Pipo's Hop Go?
summary: One morning, Pipo the little rabbit wakes to find his hop has gone; can his meadow friends help him find it again?

scenes.text: That morning, Pipo the little rabbit woke up in his burrow, sighed, and opened the door. He almost always came out hopping, but today his legs felt heavy, heavy. He didn't feel like jumping. Outside, the meadow waited for him, golden with sun, and the breeze moved the leaves. Pipo only took one small step and sat down. “Where did my hop go?” he wondered, looking at his feet. In his chest there was a gray cloud, and he didn't know how to push it aside.

Very soon, yellow and round as a drop of sun, a bee arrived with her buzz. “Good morning, Pipo,” she said, spinning circles in the air. “Come see the new flowers, they all opened last night.” Pipo didn't feel much like it, but she was so cheerful that he followed her with a few slow steps. The grass tickled his paws. Among the flowers there were beads of dew that shone like tiny diamonds. “You don't have to jump yet,” the bee told him sweetly. “Just walk with me.” And Pipo, without noticing, smiled for the first time all day.

On a mossy stone, beside the clear water, there waited a green frog. “Hi, Pipo,” she greeted him with a croak. “Watch what I can do.” She took a huge jump and splash!, she landed right in the middle of the puddle. The drops leaped everywhere and Pipo smiled without meaning to. “You try,” said the frog. The little rabbit came closer slowly and dipped in one paw. The water was cool and it tickled him. He dipped in the other, and then both. He paddled carefully, very slowly, and felt something warm begin to wake up inside his chest.

The sun was high now and a warm breeze stroked his ears. The bee, the frog, and Pipo played among the flowers all morning. And then, without thinking, a hop popped right out of Pipo. A tiny one! Then a bigger one, and another, and another. His legs didn't feel heavy anymore: they were flying. The little rabbit opened his mouth wide and out came his big, round, long-lost laugh. “My hop came back!” he cried happily. His friends hopped with him, and the whole meadow seemed to join in, swaying with the wind.

When the sky turned peach-colored, out of the tallest tree peeked an owl. “It's time to rest, little ones,” he said in a soft voice. Pipo said goodbye to the bee and the frog with a hug. He went back to his burrow in tired, happy hops. He curled up, closed his eyes, and breathed in deep, very deep. Up above, one by one, out came the stars. They were like warm lights wishing him good night. Pipo no longer carried the gray cloud in his chest. He knew that sometimes joy hides for a while, but always, always comes back. And he fell asleep dreaming of tomorrow's hop.
